description:
pkix-ct/src/log_list.rs:42-46
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:837-857

Docstring says:

> `None` means the log has never reached the `usable` state.

Implementation in `log_window_contains` treats `None` as "unbounded
lower bound — every SCT timestamp passes":

```rust
if let Some(lo) = log.usable_from_ms {
    if timestamp_ms < lo {
        return false;
    }
}
// fallthrough: pass
```

These two interpretations are contradictory. PKIX-ppbr.1 already filed
this as a bug to fix. The api-contract angle is that `Option<u64>`
is the wrong TYPE for what the field needs to express, regardless of
which interpretation the bugfix picks.

The contract has three distinct states the caller cares about:

1. Log has reached `usable`, and a precise `usable_from_ms` is known.
2. Log has been observed in the log-list source but has not yet
   reached `usable` — every SCT signed by it is untrusted.
3. Log-list source did not encode a timestamp, but the log is in
   `usable`/`readonly`/`retired` — caller wants permissive behavior
   (don't reject just because metadata is missing).

`Option<u64>` collapses (2) and (3) into the same value. The Google
log_list.json schema actually does distinguish them: a log with state
`pending` has no `usable.timestamp` because it never became usable; a
log with state `usable` always has `usable.timestamp` because the
schema requires it.

Recommendation: replace with a typed `LogTrustWindow` (PKIX-ppbr.1
will need to choose anyway). Sketch:

```rust
pub enum LogTrustWindow {
    NeverTrusted,
    UsableFromMs(u64),
    UsableFromMsUntilMs(u64, u64),
    UnboundedTimes,  // permissive default, callers can opt in
}
```

Or carry the schema state explicitly: `state: LogState` where
`LogState::{Pending, Qualified, Usable {ts}, ReadOnly, Retired {ts},
Rejected}`. That's also the fix for PKIX-ppbr.2.

This is also a partial fix for non-negotiable #5's framework-policy
split: the spec defines six states; the workspace currently picks two
fields and hopes they cover the cases.

Priority P1 because the bug fix in PKIX-ppbr.1 is going to touch this
type signature; the contract decision should be made jointly.
title: CtLog::usable_from_ms: None has two conflicting documented meanings — Option<u64> wrong type
